coverage_gaps: Only PubMed is available, so non-indexed primary literature and records exclusive to other biomedical indexes may be missed.
Dedicated citation-graph services are unavailable; backward and forward citation expansion can only be approximated through PubMed records, related articles, authors, and terminology.

Human variant databases, population-frequency resources, and curated clinical-interpretation repositories are unavailable, limiting independent verification of variant classification and ancestry-specific frequency.
Preprint servers are unavailable, so recent unreviewed mechanistic findings through 2024-12-31 may be undercovered.
Trial registries and regulatory sources are unavailable; clinical development, inhibitor safety, and regulatory status cannot be comprehensively assessed.
Patent and chemistry sources are unavailable, limiting coverage of substrate-assay intellectual history and inhibitor prior art.
PubMed indexing and abstract availability may underrepresent negative experiments, unpublished failed replications, and full methodological details.
exclusion_criteria: Records mentioning LRRK2 only incidentally without evidence relevant to the genetic or mechanistic question are excluded.
Studies limited to unrelated diseases are excluded unless they directly inform conserved LRRK2 enzymology, physiological substrates, or tissue-dependent mechanism.
Purely computational predictions of pathogenicity, structure, or substrates without experimental or human genetic support are excluded from claim confirmation.
Overexpression-only substrate claims lacking direct phosphorylation evidence or an endogenous, genetic, or pharmacological dependency test are excluded from designation as physiological substrates.
Narrative reviews, editorials, and commentaries are excluded as sole support for factual claims, while their terminology and cited primary studies may guide expansion.
Records published after 2024-12-31 are excluded from the brief and reserved for a future update.
Duplicate canonical records are merged by PMID or DOI while preserving all query-to-record links; conflicting duplicate metadata is flagged and withheld pending resolution.
Retracted studies are excluded from positive support and retained only to document limitations or provenance.
inclusion_criteria: Publication date is on or before 2024-12-31; ambiguous online-first and issue dates are checked against the cutoff after retrieval.

The record directly addresses LRRK2/PARK8 and Parkinson disease genetics, variant biology, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrates, relevant cellular physiology, or evidence limiting those claims.

Primary human genetic, biochemical, structural, cellular, animal-model, neuropathological, or human-biospecimen studies are eligible; systematic or authoritative reviews are retained for terminology and reference expansion.

Mechanistic studies without a Parkinson disease cohort are eligible when they test endogenous LRRK2, a disease-associated LRRK2 variant, or a proposed physiological substrate in a disease-relevant system.

Substrate claims must report direct phosphorylation, mapped sites, endogenous perturbation, genetic dependence, inhibitor sensitivity, or orthogonal validation sufficient to classify the evidentiary basis.
Null, negative, contradictory, replication, penetrance, correction, and retraction records are eligible when they bear on causal strength or generality.
No language restriction is applied at retrieval; final inclusion requires enough interpretable title, abstract, or full-text information to evaluate methods and conclusions.
All retained claims must preserve the PubMed identifier and every query-to-record occurrence for deduplication and replay.

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: from PubMed database inception through 2024-12-31, assess how human genetic evidence links LRRK2 to Parkinson disease, which disease-associated variants alter kinase or ROC-COR GTPase functions, which Rab proteins or other candidates qualify as physiological substrates, how these molecular effects connect to cellular and organismal phenotypes, and which penetrance, replication, model-dependence, pathological heterogeneity, or null evidence limits causal strength or generality. Scope includes human genetic, biochemical, structural, cellular, animal-model, neuropathological, and human-biospecimen studies; reviews are used for terminology and citation leads, with decision claims traced to primary studies.
stop_rules: Complete all twelve planned PubMed query events and record each exact query, retrieval timestamp, requested cutoff, result count, and available provider metadata.

Confirm recovery of both the early PARK8/LRRK2 discovery line and an anchor Rab-substrate discovery line; if either is missing, expand aliases and rerun the affected sentinel branch within the query budget.

Continue screening until each required domain has at least one assessable primary evidence set: genetic discovery, variant spectrum, enzymatic mechanism, physiological substrate evidence, disease-relevant physiology, human validation, and limiting evidence.

Stop expansion after two consecutive reviewed expansion batches add no decision-relevant primary study, new disease-associated variant class, new validated substrate class, or material challenge to the mechanism.
Stop when additional PubMed retrieval cannot reasonably change the calibrated conclusions about genetic causality, variant-dependent enzymology, substrate status, or generalizability.
If the maximum of twelve query events is reached before saturation, stop and report budget exhaustion together with unresolved evidence domains.
Apply the 2024-12-31 cutoff after retrieval when PubMed date fields are ambiguous and stop the update wave only after all eligible records through that date are screened.
